title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
source_notes: Primary-source fetch of nvlpubs.nist.gov was denied (permission prompt timed out) on 2026-11-23; rows compiled from knowledge of the published text and must be verified against source_url before this table is upgraded to primary.

rows.title: Cultivate and implement a culture of AI risk management
Policies, processes and practices for AI risk management are in place
Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood and documented
Trustworthy AI characteristics integrated into organizational policies
Processes determine needed risk management level based on risk tolerance
Risk management process established through transparent policies and controls
Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process
Mechanisms to inventory AI systems
Processes for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems
Accountability structures empower and train teams for AI risk management
Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication are documented
Personnel and partners receive AI risk management training
Executive leadership takes responsibility for AI risk decisions
Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility are prioritized
Risk decisions informed by a diverse team
Policies defining roles for human-AI configurations and oversight
Teams committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk
Policies foster critical thinking and a safety-first mindset
Teams document and communicate risks and impacts of AI technology
Practices enable AI testing, incident identification and information sharing
Robust engagement with relevant AI actors
Collect and integrate external feedback on individual and societal impacts
Mechanisms to incorporate adjudicated feedback into system design
Policies addressing third-party software, data and supply-chain risks
Policies address AI risks associated with third-party entities
Contingency processes for failures in high-risk third-party data or systems
Establish context to frame AI risks
Context is established and understood
Intended purposes, context-specific laws, norms and deployment settings documented
Interdisciplinary and diverse AI actors establish context
Organizational mission and goals for AI technology are documented
Business value or context of business use is clearly defined
Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented
System requirements elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors
Categorization of the AI system is performed
Specific tasks and implementation methods of the AI system are defined
Knowledge limits and human use and oversight of outputs documented
Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented
AI capabilities, usage, goals, benefits and costs are understood
Potential benefits of intended AI functionality are examined and documented
Potential costs, including non-monetary costs of AI errors, documented
Targeted application scope is specified and documented
Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency are defined
Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed and documented
Risks and benefits mapped for all components including third-party
Approaches for mapping technology and legal risks of components documented
Internal risk controls for AI system components are identified
Impacts to individuals, groups, communities and society are characterized
Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact are documented
Practices for regular engagement and impact feedback are in place
Analyze, assess, benchmark and monitor AI risk and impacts
Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied
Measurement approaches and metrics selected starting with significant risks
Appropriateness of metrics and effectiveness of controls regularly assessed
Independent assessors involved in regular assessments and updates
AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics
Test sets, metrics and TEVV tool details are documented
Human-subject evaluations meet requirements and are representative
Performance or assurance criteria measured for deployment-like conditions
AI system functionality and behavior monitored in production
AI system is demonstrated to be valid and reliable
AI system evaluated for safety risks and can fail safely
AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented
Transparency and accountability risks are examined and documented
AI model is explained, validated and documented
Privacy risk of the AI system is examined and documented
Fairness and bias are evaluated and results documented
Environmental impact and sustainability are assessed and documented
Effectiveness of TEVV metrics and processes is evaluated
Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place
Existing, unanticipated and emergent AI risks are regularly tracked
Risk tracking considered where risks are difficult to measure
Feedback processes for end users to report problems and appeal outcomes
Feedback about efficacy of measurement is gathered and assessed
Measurement approaches connected to deployment context and domain experts
Trustworthiness measurement results validated with domain experts and AI actors
Measurable performance improvements or declines are identified and documented
Allocate resources to mapped and measured AI risks
AI risks from MAP and MEASURE are prioritized, responded to and managed
Determine whether AI system achieves purpose and should proceed
Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized
Responses to high-priority AI risks are developed and documented
Negative residual risks to acquirers and end users are documented
Strategies to maximize AI benefits and minimize negative impacts
Resources and non-AI alternatives considered to reduce impacts
Mechanisms to sustain the value of deployed AI systems
Procedures to respond to and recover from previously unknown risks
Mechanisms to supersede, disengage or deactivate AI systems
AI risks and benefits from third-party entities are managed
Third-party AI risks regularly monitored and risk controls applied
Pre-trained models used for development are monitored
Risk treatments and communication plans are documented and monitored
Post-deployment monitoring plans, including appeal, override and decommissioning
Measurable continual improvement activities integrated into AI system updates
Incidents and errors are communicated, tracked and recovered from
